title: altdown 0.0.0.9000
text:
A toy function that returns a greeting message. Used only to give this example package something to document.



greet(name = "world", loud = FALSE)






name


A character string with the name to greet.




loud


Logical. If ‘TRUE’, the greeting is shouted (all caps).






A character string with the greeting.




greet("world")
#> [1] "Hello, world!"
greet("world", loud = TRUE)
#> [1] "HELLO, WORLD!"

title: altdown 0.0.0.9000
text:
Writes altdoc/altdown.yml, the one configuration file build_site() reads, with a starter reference: field listing every function currently documented in <path>/man/*.Rd in one "All functions" section. Also adds the .gitignore/.Rbuildignore entries the build needs (see Details) if they’re not already there.



use_altdown(path = ".")






path


Path to the target package root. Defaults to the current directory.






An existing altdoc/altdown.yml is never overwritten. If the package was set up with an earlier version of altdown, the reference: field is taken over from its altdoc/reference.yml; that file, and the altdoc/build-site.R and altdoc/quarto_website_static.yml copies, are no longer used and can be deleted.
use_altdown() adds the following lines to .gitignore and .Rbuildignore (only the ones not already present in each file):

# .gitignore
_quarto/*
!_quarto/_freeze/
altdoc/freeze.rds
altdoc/pkgdown.yml
altdoc/quarto_website.yml
altdoc/index.md
altdoc/reference.qmd
altdoc/authors.qmd
altdoc/altdown.scss
altdoc/altdown-header.html
altdoc/altdown-after-body.html
altdoc/altdown-pre-render.R

# .Rbuildignore
^docs\$
^altdoc\$
^_quarto\$


The first four mirror what altdoc::setup_docs(tool = "quarto_website") adds, plus altdoc/pkgdown.yml, which altdoc::render_docs() rewrites on every build. The rest are the files build_site() generates.



Invisibly, the path to the altdoc/ directory.




pkg <- tempfile("examplepkg")
dir.create(pkg)
write(
  "Package: examplepkg\nVersion: 0.0.0.9000",
  file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION")
)
use_altdown(pkg)
list.files(file.path(pkg, "altdoc"))
#> [1] "altdown.yml"
unlink(pkg, recursive = TRUE)

title: Getting started with altdown
text:
This vignette shows off a few Quarto callout blocks, and how they render on a site built with altdoc’s quarto_website tool, which lets Quarto handle vignettes directly instead of converting them to plain Markdown first.
greet() and add() below are not part of the real package API; they are toy functions injected during the site build for this showcase (see the reference index).
library(altdown)

title: Getting started with altdown
text:
Saying hello






Note



greet() is a toy demo function; it just pastes together a friendly string. Nothing fancy.



greet("altdoc")

[1] "Hello, altdoc!"


You can also shout the greeting:

greet("altdoc", loud = TRUE)

[1] "HELLO, ALTDOC!"








TipTip



Set loud = TRUE when you really mean it.

title: Getting started with altdown
text:
Adding numbers

add(2, 40)

[1] 42








Warning



Like greet(), add() is a toy stand-in: it does no input validation, so passing non-numeric arguments raises a base R error rather than a friendly one.



add("2", 40)

Error in `x + y`:
! non-numeric argument to binary operator

title: altdown 0.0.0.9000
text:
altdown 0.0.0.9000

New build_site() builds the site; the build logic, theme and scripts now live in the package instead of being copied into altdoc/.
use_altdown() now only writes altdoc/altdown.yml, which holds the reference: grouping (taken over from an existing altdoc/reference.yml) and optional articles: and quarto: fields. Its overwrite argument is gone.
build_site() no longer modifies README.md, and lists every vignette other than the “Get started” one under “Articles”.
build_site() adds reftip tooltips when reftip is installed.
Initial release.

title: altdown
text:
Browse source code
Report a bug



Full license
MIT + file LICENSE



Contributing guide



Citing altdown



Bjarke Hautop Kristensen
Author, maintainer



 

altdown is an R package that provides a theme for altdoc websites built with Quarto, styled to mirror the output of pkgdown (Bootstrap 5).


Install from GitHub:
pak::pak("https://github.com/BjarkeHautop/altdown")



Browse around to see how it looks! If you like what you see, and want to use it for your own package, run:
altdown::use_altdown()
This writes altdoc/altdown.yml, with a reference: field that lists your package’s current functions in one section; edit it to group them however you’d like, in the same shape as pkgdown’s reference: field. It also gitignores the files the build generates.
Then build the site:
altdown::build_site()
A preview can then be viewed using altdoc::preview_docs().
The navbar is built from your vignettes: the one named after the package (or the only top-level one) becomes “Get started”, and the rest, including those in vignettes/articles/, go under “Articles”. If reftip is installed, build_site() also adds hover tooltips to references to your package’s functions. See ?altdown::build_site for everything altdown.yml can configure.



reftip adds hover tooltips to the function reference links that altdoc creates in a rendered R code block; build_site() runs it automatically when it’s installed. alttip shows an example site using altdown and reftip together.



pkgdown supports Quarto (see vignette("quarto")), but the way it’s implemented is hard to maintain and lags behind in features. For instance, callout blocks, code annotations, and tabsets don’t work correctly. Callout blocks are what I personally wanted most, since I’ve grown fond of them.
This happens because pkgdown hardcodes theme: "none" and minimal: TRUE so it can supply its own CSS instead of Quarto’s, which strips the callout, annotation, and tabset styling. Callouts, for instance, get converted to plain blockquotes.
The fix would be patching pkgdown itself, but it’s a bit more involved than one would first think. The tldr is you have to merge two competing asset systems, which is not trivial. Hence I use altdoc, and manually construct my layout for something that looks like pkgdown.

title: Technical details
text:
This page explains how the site is put together. It is a Quarto website built with altdoc, with some extra styling and JavaScript to make it look like a pkgdown (Bootstrap 5) site.
The only file a package keeps in altdoc/ is altdown.yml. Everything else there is written by altdown::build_site() on every build, and gitignored:

title: Technical details
text:
Why generate files?
For a Quarto backend, the intended approach is to modify the source files with a script and then call altdoc::render_docs() yourself (see altdoc’s customization vignette).
That is what build_site() does. altdoc copies altdoc/ into its Quarto project, so files written there before altdoc::render_docs() end up in the site. The main ones are explained below.

The home page
altdoc’s home page is an index.md that includes README.md. Since altdoc copies altdoc/ into its Quarto project after importing the README, build_site() writes its own altdoc/index.md to replace it: the README with a .column-margin sidebar, matching pkgdown’s layout, with the README’s badges moved into it. README.md itself is never modified.


The reference index
altdoc does not currently have a _pkgdown.yml-style reference: field for controlling how the function index is grouped and ordered (etiennebacher/altdoc#326).
So altdoc/altdown.yml has a reference: field, using the same basic structure as pkgdown’s. build_site() uses it together with the \name{} and \alias{} entries in man/*.Rd to generate altdoc/reference.qmd.


The navbar and footer
altdoc/quarto_website.yml is generated in full: the navbar links the “Get started” vignette, the reference index, the other vignettes under “Articles” and the changelog, and the footer has the “Developed by .” text used by pkgdown, based on Authors@R. A quarto: field in altdown.yml is merged over it.


The man pages
altdoc converts each man/*.Rd file to a .qmd page during altdoc::render_docs(), and renders the Quarto project straight after, so build_site() can’t edit those pages beforehand. Instead altdown-pre-render.R runs as a Quarto pre-render script, inside that render. It turns the Usage section into a highlighted R code block, rewrites inline <code> as Markdown code spans (so Pandoc doesn’t turn their " into curly quotes), and turns examples that aren’t run (\dontrun{}) into plain code blocks, so those pages don’t need knitr and a separate R session each.

title: Technical details
text:
Matching the pkgdown look
altdown.scss is a Quarto theme layer:
theme: [default, altdown.scss]
It is based on pkgdown’s own pkgdown.scss, but the selectors have been adapted to Quarto’s HTML.
It does the following:

Limiting the navbar to a centered, fixed-width container.
Putting the navbar items (title, links, search, GitHub icon) in the same order as pkgdown.
Styling the margin sidebar and reference index (<dl class="ref-index">) to look like their pkgdown counterparts.

There is one annoying thing that can’t be fixed though: the navbar title does not line up with the body text automatically. Quarto uses a different layout for the home page, so the body’s left edge is not in the same place on every page. Therefore, the generated quarto_website.yml includes a small include-after-body script that measures the actual offset after the page has loaded and adjusts the navbar padding accordingly.

title: altdown 0.0.0.9000
text:
Builds the package website into docs/ with altdoc::render_docs(), styled to mirror pkgdown. Before rendering it generates, from the package sources and altdoc/altdown.yml:



build_site(
  path = ".",
  tooltips = requireNamespace("reftip", quietly = TRUE),
  ...
)






path


Path to the package root.




tooltips


Logical. Add hover tooltips to references to the package’s own functions with reftip::add_tooltips()? Defaults to TRUE when reftip is installed.




...


Passed on to altdoc::render_docs(), e.g. freeze or parallel.








the navbar, with a "Get started" link, the function reference, an "Articles" menu and the changelog;


the home page, built from README.md plus a pkgdown-style sidebar (links, license, citation, developers and the README’s badges);


the grouped function reference index;


the "Authors and Citation" page.


These generated files are written to altdoc/ (which altdoc copies into its Quarto project), so they’re gitignored by use_altdown(). README.md itself is never modified.



Invisibly, the path to the built site.



altdoc/altdown.yml (created by use_altdown()) can contain:


reference: groups the function reference index, in the same shape as pkgdown’s reference: field. contents entries can be a topic alias or a selector: starts_with(), ends_with(), contains(), matches(), has_concept(), has_keyword(), - to exclude, and c() to combine. Without it, every topic is listed in one section.


articles: the order of the "Articles" navbar menu, as vignette paths relative to vignettes/ without extension (e.g. articles/details). Without it, every vignette other than the "Get started" one is listed, top-level vignettes first, then those in vignettes/articles/.


quarto: settings merged (with utils::modifyList()) over the generated Quarto configuration, e.g. to add navbar entries or extra SCSS files.


The "Get started" link points to the vignette named after the package, or to the only top-level vignette if there is just one.
